what_its_for: Bimatoprost is used to lower high pressure in your eye, which helps treat a condition called glaucoma or ocular hypertension. Lowering eye pressure helps prevent vision loss. It is also used (as Latisse) to help grow longer, thicker, and darker eyelashes.
how_to_take: For eye drops (Lumigan): Wash your hands before use. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to form a small pocket, and place one drop into the affected eye. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye to keep the medicine from draining out. Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye, fingers, or any surface. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. For eyelash treatment (Latisse): Apply one drop to the applicator brush provided and carefully draw it along the upper eyelid at the base of your eyelashes. Do not apply it to your lower lid. Use a fresh applicator for each eye. Blot away any extra solution.
dosing: For glaucoma (Lumigan): Use one drop in the affected eye or eyes once every evening, usually at bedtime. For eyelash growth (Latisse): Apply once each evening. Do not use more than once a day, as using it more often will not make it work better and may increase side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not use two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children. Do not freeze. Throw away the bottle 4 weeks after you first open it, even if there is still medicine left inside.
what_to_avoid: Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface, including your eye or skin, to prevent contamination. Do not use more drops than prescribed. Avoid driving or using machinery right after applying the drops until your vision clears. Be aware that bimatoprost can permanently darken the color of your iris (the colored part of your eye) and the skin around your eye. It can also cause increased growth or darkening of eyelashes. To reduce unwanted hair growth or skin darkening, wipe off any extra solution that gets on your skin.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: sudden vision changes or loss of vision, eye pain, redness, or irritation that is severe or does not go away, signs of an eye infection such as discharge or swelling, swelling around the eye, chest pain, or any new or unusual symptoms. Also call your doctor if you notice unusual darkening of the skin around your eye or a change in your eye color.
when_it_works: For glaucoma, bimatoprost usually starts lowering eye pressure within 4 hours of your first dose, and the full effect is often seen within 8 to 12 hours. For eyelash growth, you may start to see results in as little as 4 weeks, but full results usually take about 16 weeks (4 months) of regular use.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine. Use in children should only be done under a doctor's close supervision. If you have a history of eye surgery, eye inflammation, or macular edema (swelling in the back of the eye), tell your doctor before starting bimatoprost. People who use only one eye drop should be careful to avoid getting the medicine in the other eye, as it may affect eyelash growth and eye color in both eyes.
